campaignAudits.trigger: Marcel asked whether the other scheduled batches had gone out. Nobody had audited campaign state since they were built.
campaignAudits.finding: Campaign 618477, Play 0 batch 1, was recorded in this repo as 'dead, never to resume' after it wedged in STARTING on 2026-09-23. That was WRONG. It resumed, and by 2026-09-25 it showed 4 finished with MessageSent, 5 excluded and 1 in sequence, running alongside 618489, the rebuild, which covers the same ten people.
campaignAudits.feared: That Narvaez, Tavares, Arredondo and Ohad Gold had each received the same Play 0 message twice.
campaignAudits.actual: NO DUPLICATE WAS DELIVERED. The conversation threads were checked one by one: Fernando Narvaez has 1 message, Alan Arredondo has 1, Elena Tavares has 3 but only one dated 2026-09-24. HeyReach's two campaign records point at the same underlying send and the platform deduplicated at the conversation level.
campaignAudits.actionTaken: Paused 618477 and manually stopped Ohad Gold in 618489. Both were correct regardless: every one of 618477's ten people is covered by 618489, Jennifer Ayers had already been messaged by 618489 at 01:26, and Ohad Gold had already been messaged by 618477 at 19:55. Nothing useful was lost and nothing was at risk of going twice.
campaignAudits.lesson: Two rules out of this. First, PAUSED IS NOT DEAD. A campaign that wedges and gets paused can resume; the repo said 618477 would never run again and it ran. Verify campaign state, do not carry an assumption forward. Second, CAMPAIGN STATS ARE NOT THE TRUTH, THE THREAD IS. Two campaigns can both report MessageSent for one actual message. Before telling Marcel someone was double contacted, open the conversation and count.
